questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Poland?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter W and has 6 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Poland article.

questions.proof: Most Polish people live in large cities, including the capital, Warsaw (Polish: Warszawa), Łódź, Cracow (Polish: Kraków), the second capital of Poland (first was Gniezno), Szczecin, Gdańsk, Wrocław and Poznań.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Poland?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter B and has 7 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Poland article.

questions.proof: The Czech Republic and Slovakia are to the south, Ukraine and Belarus to the east, and the Baltic Sea, Lithuania, and the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad to the north.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Poland?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter P and has 6 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Literature” part of the Poland article.

questions.proof: Polish literature was written in the Latin language during the Middle Ages.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “After the death of Casimir the Great, the last Piast on the Polish throne, Louis I of _____ and his daughter Jadwiga of Poland began their rule.”

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter H and has 7 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Piast and Jagiellon dynasties” part of the Poland article.

questions.proof: After the death of Casimir the Great, the last Piast on the Polish throne, Louis I of Hungary and his daughter Jadwiga of Poland began their rule.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The total land area of Poland is about 312,679 km2 (120,728 mi2), slightly larger than _____.”

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter O and has 4 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Poland article.

questions.proof: The total land area of Poland is about 312,679 km2 (120,728 mi2), slightly larger than Oman.
